CONFIRM C0039 — `_create_sandbox()` derives `common = os.path.commonpath(all_paths)`. When `source_paths` is a single file, `common` becomes that file’s path, then is normalized to its parent directory, so sibling imports above that directory are excluded. This breaks the stated invariant “preserving package structure” and can make pyright/mypy resolution fail in the sandbox for valid fixes. Using a stable project root or copying a wider tree is the simplest correct repair.

CONFIRM C0040 — `line_pattern = re.compile(r"[Ll]ines?\s+(\d+)(?:\s*[-–]\s*(\d+))?:\s*(.+?)\s*->\s*(.+)")` does not use `re.DOTALL`, so Strategy 3 cannot match multi-line old/new fragments after `:` or `->`. That makes a common model output form for block edits unevaluable.

CONFIRM C0041 — response-size anomaly emits `signal_type="context_growth"` in check 4 even though the detail and threshold concern per-model oversized outputs, not cumulative context fraction. This mislabels the signal and can make downstream routing treat the wrong condition as firing.

CHALLENGE C0031 | `tools_available` is a local dict initialized fresh inside each `scan_health()` call, so there is no persisted “already known unavailable” state to skip against. The code does not currently retain cross-run availability knowledge. The proposed fix cannot work as written and the issue is not a real defect in this file’s current behavior.

CHALLENGE C0033 | The mapping `LOW -> info`, `MEDIUM -> warning`, `HIGH -> error` is internally consistent with the module’s own severity vocabulary and aggregation logic. There is no evidence in `endocrine.py` that the insect brain or immune pipeline interprets endocrine severities as a binary high/low gate where this becomes silently wrong. This is calibration preference, not a PoC bug.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.96
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `run_pyright()` silently drops all diagnostics when pyright exits nonzero with valid-but-partial JSON on stdout and any non-empty stderr. The code only treats `stderr == "NOT_FOUND"` as exceptional, otherwise it attempts `json.loads(result.stdout)` and, on parse failure, logs a warning then returns `[]`. Pyright commonly emits config/import/runtime errors via stderr while also failing the JSON contract; this path is interpreted as “no diagnostics”. Evidence: `run_pyright()` has no returncode check, no `TIMEOUT` handling beyond the generic parse failure, and no error sentinel; `scan_health()` then aggregates an empty list as a healthy tool result.
FOLLOW: This creates silently wrong health scans: type-check failures disappear from `HealthScan.total`, `counts_by_tool`, and `counts_by_category`. Because `evaluate_fix()` also uses `run_pyright()` via `_count_tool_issues()`, fix evaluation can mark broken fixes as SAFE/NEUTRAL when pyright actually failed to run or report. That directly undermines two advertised endocrine features: health scan and fix evaluation.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — In `run_pyright()`, treat `result.returncode == -1`, `result.stderr == "TIMEOUT"`, empty/non-JSON stdout on nonzero exit, or JSON parse failure as tool failure by raising `RuntimeError` (or `ToolNotFoundError` only for NOT_FOUND). Do not return `[]` on parse failure.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.93
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `run_bandit()` has the same fail-open behavior as `run_pyright()`: if bandit times out, crashes, or emits malformed/non-JSON output, the function catches `JSONDecodeError` and returns an empty diagnostics list. It only special-cases `stderr == "NOT_FOUND"`. Evidence: `data = json.loads(result.stdout) if result.stdout.strip() else {}` followed by `except ...: logger.warning(...)`; no returncode or timeout handling besides NOT_FOUND.
FOLLOW: Health scan can report zero security findings when bandit did not run successfully. In fix evaluation, `_count_tool_issues(run_bandit, ...)` turns tool execution failures into zero new issues, allowing harmful fixes to look SAFE/NEUTRAL. This is a silent wrong-result path, not just missing telemetry.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — In `run_bandit()`, raise on timeout/nonzero execution that does not yield valid JSON, instead of returning `[]`. Keep only the explicit NOT_FOUND case as `ToolNotFoundError`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.92
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `run_ruff()` also fails open on execution/parsing errors. It checks only `stderr == "NOT_FOUND"`, then does `issues = json.loads(result.stdout) if result.stdout.strip() else []`; malformed output or timeout becomes a logged warning plus `[]`. There is no returncode validation and no timeout-specific failure propagation.
FOLLOW: Ruff outages are misclassified as “no lint/style/bugbear/security findings”. In fix evaluation this suppresses regressions and can produce incorrect SAFE/NEUTRAL verdicts. Because fix verification relies on before/after counts, a dead ruff invocation makes the comparison meaningless while still appearing successful.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — In `run_ruff()`, raise on timeout or invalid/non-JSON output instead of returning an empty list. Successful empty output should remain `[]`; unsuccessful execution should propagate as failure.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.90
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `EndocrineLayer.run()` does not surface any result for the advertised “defect detection” capability. The module docstring and top-level design describe four functions including “Defect detect — classify findings by defect category”, but `EndocrineReport` contains only `health_scan`, `fix_evaluations`, and `pacing_signals`, and `run()` computes only those three. The only category data available is incidental aggregation inside `HealthScan`, not a distinct detection pass or interface consumable from the coordinator.
FOLLOW: The insect brain integration cannot consume a standalone defect-detection output because none exists. For a PoC whose purpose is “all significant features firing cleanly,” one declared feature is effectively dead as a public capability: nothing in the coordinator executes or returns it as a first-class result.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Add a dedicated `defect_detection` field to `EndocrineReport` and populate it in `run()` from the collected diagnostics using the existing category aggregation logic, exposing the feature as an explicit coordinator output.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.82
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.39
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()` novelty plateau threshold is internally inconsistent: the comment says “If novelty has been zero or near-zero for 3 consecutive rounds,” but the signal threshold is stored as `float(window)` i.e. `3.0`, while the actual predicate is `all(n <= 1 for n in recent)`. The reported threshold does not correspond to the decision rule or metric (`sum(recent)`).
FOLLOW: Downstream consumers or logs inspecting `metric_value` versus `threshold` get misleading data. Example: recent `[1,1,1]` triggers the plateau, `metric_value=3.0`, `threshold=3.0`, which looks exactly at threshold even though the real trigger was per-round `<=1`. This corrupts pacing explainability and makes debugging or tuning the signal harder.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Set the novelty plateau threshold metadata to match the rule actually used, e.g. `threshold=1.0` with detail clarifying “per-round novelty <= 1 for last 3 rounds”.
VERIFIED: TRUE
